theorem.input: Graph C with exact lists L(v) subseteq [4] and a cut vertex r.
theorem.components: Let Q_1,...,Q_t be the connected components of C-r.
theorem.boundary_lists: For kappa in L(r), define L_i^kappa(v)=L(v)\{kappa} if vr is an edge, otherwise L(v).
theorem.equivalence: C is list-colorable iff there exists kappa in L(r) such that every (Q_i,L_i^kappa) is list-colorable.

proof.forward: Restrict any list-coloring c of C to kappa=c(r) and to each Q_i. Neighbors of r cannot use kappa, hence each restriction respects L_i^kappa.
proof.reverse: Choose kappa and a list-coloring of every Q_i under L_i^kappa. Since distinct Q_i have no edges between them, their colorings glue with r=kappa to a proper list-coloring of C.

theorem.reconstruction: Union the independently reconstructed component colorings and set r=kappa.
theorem.complexity_overhead: At most |L(r)|<=4 boundary branches plus linear-time component construction and list restriction; downstream complexity is the sum of the chosen component solvers.

proof_carrying_certificate.cut_vertex: Verify C-r has at least two connected components.
proof_carrying_certificate.component_partition: Verify components partition V(C)\{r} and there are no inter-component edges.
proof_carrying_certificate.per_kappa: Preserve exact restricted lists and each downstream component certificate.
proof_carrying_certificate.branch_result: A kappa branch is SAT iff all components are SAT; it is rejected if any component is contradiction/UNSAT.
